title: DSS triage record
description: Proposal, not yet agreed by both owners. One record per DSS ticket: dss_ticket is filled by code, triage and class by Claude, resolved by a person after the DSS ticket closes. The design is on the DSS Triage Flow page.

dss_ticket.description: Facts as they were when the DSS ticket was filed, each built by code.

project.description: The project folder on the share.

prod_version.description: Prod when the DSS ticket was filed.

last_error.description: The last failed session's error text.

terminal_log.description: That session's terminal log, which Cerberus writes from 1.1 on: its errors before the DSS ticket (each with the end of its traceback) and warnings, each with its line number, or why there is none. Null when no session was found.

triage.description: Claude's answer; the DM and its thread reply are rendered from it.

status.description: proved when every link of the cause was read with a tool; likely when the cause fits the evidence but no tool can read one link; needs_info when the answer depends on something only the analyst can give; not_cerberus when Gate A says so.

headline.description: The verdict in a few plain words, such as "Known issue, fix coming in Cerberus 1.1", "New bug, not fixed yet", "Two bugs, neither fixed", "Input problem: casing ID differs from the tally", "One question for the analyst" or "Not Cerberus: ask the VizApp team". Name a release only when a DTN ticket's fix version names it.

actions.description: What each side should do: short instructions that start with a verb; an empty list means there is nothing to do. Never repeat a question or a not_proved check here: code adds those.

analyst.description: Correct an input (name the file, sheet and row or cell, and the value to set), update Cerberus and rerun, or wait for the release. When the cause is in their data, start with the check that shows it in their tools, then the fix, then each step to rerun in order (such as re-exporting calipers before CatCall). When Cerberus works as designed, still check the inputs the evidence shows (calipers from different passes or folders). When it is a Cerberus bug, review the output a developer regenerates from the fix branch.

developers.description: Raise a DTN ticket (say what for), set a fix version, regenerate the deliverable from a fixed branch or PR (name it), or review or merge an existing PR (name it). Give a deadline when the analyst's review date makes one matter. Only steps that confirm or fix this ticket's cause. For a custom request, the DFR steps from the rules instead of building it.

settled_at.description: The step that settled it: request (step 1), prior_art (steps 2 and 3), a gate, or a step 7 playbook.

playbook.description: Step 7's playbook; null when it settled before step 7.

what.description: The summary: what the analyst reported, in one plain sentence.

request.description: Step 1: what the analyst asks, stated before the investigation.

output.description: The output or Cerberus step where they see it.

expected.description: What they expected, when the ticket says.

prior_art.description: Steps 2 and 3: past DSS and DTN tickets, commits, branches and pages that match, and whether each one's fix applies. Empty when the searches found nothing.

ref.description: A DSS or DTN key, a commit, a branch or a page.

what.description: The past issue in one line.

why.description: The evidence for applies, such as a code_contains result.

cause.description: One sentence with its mechanism, "X was Y, so Z"; when the analyst reports several issues, one such sentence for each, in their order; null when unknown.

where.description: Where the cause lives; null when unknown.

ref.description: The tool call that read it, such as cerb_client_info:1234, code_read:cerberus/plots.py:120, slack_thread:reply 1 screenshot or terminal_log:line 1201, or 'computed'.

not_proved.description: Each link of this ticket's cause that no tool read, as the check a developer would make to settle it, such as "Read DVT4932's Perf Info dvStage for client stages 69-71 to confirm they share one DV stage". The post lists them as the developers' Confirm actions. Each settles part of this ticket's cause; leave out code changes that would not resolve it. Empty when the status is proved: a cause with an unread link is likely.

follow_ups.description: Checks after the cause is settled that do not change it: where or when a fix lands, housekeeping such as a stale file, or whether the data changed since the ticket. The post lists them as the developers' Confirm actions too.

questions.description: Only questions whose answer settles something, each saying what it settles. The post lists them as the analyst's Answer actions.

escalate.description: The existing DTN ticket that covers this problem; null when there is none. The bot writes no DTN drafts: the team writes DTN tickets with its own skill.

reply.description: The reply to the analyst, as a data developer would write it and send it as themselves: at most 4 short sentences, shaped and worded as "Writing for the analyst" says, the verdict first ("This works as intended." when it does). Leave out side facts and numbers that don't change what they do next. Give exact facts they can check (the design, stage, joint or file, the counts, the sheet and column where they see it), and only proved ones. Leave out implementation details (Cerberus code paths, functions, line numbers, libraries) and what they can already tell (their DVT or version, that there is no workaround, that their data or inputs are not at fault when it is a Cerberus bug). Name a release only from a DTN ticket's fix version. For a Cerberus bug, say you will fix it and regenerate their output for them to review; promise nothing else. When the status is needs_info, the reply asks the questions. Null when nothing should be sent yet.

secondary.description: A separate cause the analyst did not report; class is a whole class object, not a single value. Label suggestions go in class.labels, not here.

similar_dss_tickets.description: Keys of similar DSS tickets, for linking in Jira.

flags.description: What this run could not read (a tool that failed, a file it could not open).

details.description: By where it settled; {} otherwise. not_cerberus: {owner, sop}, the likely owner and the SOP link. Gate B: {version, prod_version, failed_run, config}. crash: {error, raises_at, changed_since}, the exact error text, the file:line that raises it, and whether that code changed since the analyst's version. wrong_numbers: {reported: {value, where}, expected: {value, where}, first_difference}, both values and the first input where they differ.

answered.description: What proved and likely answers must give.

class.description: Planning fields: values from the lists and keys only, never client, project or person names; safe to count and share. cause_family, feature and prevent are null while the cause is unknown.

module.description: A code path, only when proved.

known_cause.description: A slug from the known causes in the system prompt, new:<slug> for a repeatable cause not in it, or null.

impact.description: Null when the ticket does not say.

prevent.description: What would stop the next one.

prevent_note.description: One line on prevent, or leave it out.

dtn_tickets.description: DTN keys linked to the ticket or found.

labels.description: Jira's own two fields on the DSS ticket: the Toolbox Name and Investigation Outcome to set.

feature.description: Revised 2026-10-29 after sorting 45 more DSS tickets; for the team to agree.

resolved.description: Filled by a person after the DSS ticket closes; class corrected where the bot was wrong.

fixed_in.description: The release that fixed it, for code fixes.

replay.description: Replay mode only (python -m dss replay): an old ticket triaged as it stood when posted. Code fills cutoff, build, code_ref and leaks_found; Claude fills fixed_later and leaks.

cutoff.description: When the workflow posted the ticket; every tool answered as of then.

build.description: The analyst's Cerberus version in their last session before the ticket; null without one.

code_ref.description: The Cerberus commit the code tools read: the analyst's build, else the newest release by then.

fixed_later.description: Project files changed after the ticket whose version now shows the fix. The answer is written as the ticket stood then, as if not fixed; these notes say it was fixed in the file.

leaks.description: What Claude read that looked later than the ticket, and the tool call it came through.

leaks_found.description: What code found in the tool answers: the ticket's own key, later DSS tickets or dates after it, one line per call.
